single.rationale: Eton shows strong revenue momentum (105% YoY growth, 55% 3-year CAGR) with improving operating leverage as it approaches breakeven, but faces execution risk in commercializing newly acquired products (INCRELEX, GALZIN, PKU GOLIKE) and pipeline candidates (ET-600 PDUFA Feb 2026). The company operates in attractive rare disease markets with limited competition, generates positive free cash flow, and has reduced net debt, though high R&D spend and G&A growth create margin pressure in the near term.

team.thesis: Eton Pharmaceuticals has demonstrated exceptional revenue growth of 104.9% year-over-year to $80.0M in 2025 with a three-year CAGR of 55.5%, while approaching profitability as operating losses narrowed from -$2.6M to -$844,000 and operating cash flow surged to $10.5M from $969,000, driven by an asset-light model with minimal capital expenditures of $333,000 that generated $10.2M in free cash flow
